items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: This I showed to Fess Hill because I did not want to give a two-weeks notice and have the word get out that I was leaving the band

ctx.x: the back payments were in order.

But I decided that I was not going to pay any more alimony and sent a telegram to my father in Cincinnati, telling him to send me one saying come home at once. This I showed to Fess Hill because I did not want to give a two-weeks notice and have the word get out that I was leaving the band, which may have gotten back to my wife.

I figured that I would stay in Cincinnati long enough to get a divorce which was much easier to do there than it was in New York. So Beezie and I packed our few belongings and left the Apple by bus one afternoon and arrived in Cincinnati the next day. We lived with my father who had two rooms on Outter Street near Court Street. My mother was living on Court Street not far from my father, so I saw her every day. My brother was living with my father also.
